definition: Change in velocity a spacecraft can produce with its propellant. It is the currency of maneuvers.
source: Tsiolkovsky rocket equation; NASA Glenn, Beginner's Guide to Rockets

definition: Two-burn maneuver between two circular orbits that uses the minimum Δv.
source: NASA JPL, Basics of Space Flight

definition: Point of the orbit closest to the Sun.
source: NASA JPL, Basics of Space Flight

definition: Unit of distance equal to the radius of the Sun, 696,000 km.
Intensity of sunlight outside the atmosphere at 1 AU: 1,367 W/m².
Close pass by Venus that uses its gravity to change the orbit without spending propellant.
Coronal mass ejection: a cloud of plasma and magnetic field launched into space by the Sun.
Surface that emits heat into space. Its capacity grows with T⁴ (Stefan-Boltzmann law).
Time during which the spacecraft sees a ground station and can send data.
Near-polar orbit that passes over each latitude at the same local solar time.
source: NASA Earth Observatory, Catalog of Earth Satellite Orbits

definition: Mark for technologies and figures invented for the game. They are not NASA data.
